questions.question: In which year was the Vernacular Press Act passed in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1878**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Vernacular Press Act of 1878 was a significant piece of legislation in British India, introduced to **suppress the growing influence of Indian-language newspapers. **
 
• It sought to impose restrictions on the press, particularly targeting vernacular publications that were critical of British rule.
 
• Key Provisions of the Act
 
 
• **Registration and Licensing: **The Vernacular Press Act required vernacular newspapers to register with the government. Any publication deemed seditious or inflammatory could be suspended or banned.
 
• **Power to Censor: **The Act gave district magistrates the power to censor the content of vernacular newspapers. They could prohibit the publication of any articles that they considered objectionable.
 
• **Penalties for Violations: **Offenders could face fines, confiscation of property, and imprisonment for publishing content deemed threatening to public order or government authority.
 
 
 
• The opposition to the Act became a rallying point for Indian leaders and the nationalist movement. Prominent figures, such as Bal Gangadhar Tilak, were vocal against the Act, highlighting the need for freedom of expression.
 
• The Vernacular Press Act was eventually** repealed in 1881,** largely due to the sustained pressure from Indian nationalists and the growing recognition of the need for a more liberal approach to press freedom.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• Pongal is a traditional harvest festival celebrated in** Tamil Nadu**, typically in mid-January.
 
• It is dedicated to the **Sun God, Surya**, and marks the end of the harvest season.

• **Shivaratri:**

questions.question: Which classical dance-drama from Kerala is renowned for its vibrant makeup, elaborate costumes, and exaggerated facial expressions, often depicting stories from the Ramayana?

__
 
• Kathakali is a** classical dance-drama from Kerala**, known for its intricate and colorful makeup and costumes.
 
• It combines dance, drama, music, and elaborate **facial expressions to narrate stories**, primarily from the **Ramayana and Mahabharata.**
 
• The performance involves intense training in physical movement,** gestures (mudras), and facial expressions (abhinaya).**
 
• Kathakali artists often** wear elaborate costumes and masks,** enhancing the visual spectacle of the performances.
 
• It is performed in a highly stylized manner, emphasizing storytelling through a blend of music, rhythm, and expression.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kathak:**

 
 
• Kathak is a classical dance form from **North India(primarily Uttar Pradesh)**, characterized by intricate footwork, spins, and expressive gestures.
 
• It tells stories through expressive movements and is heavily influenced by Mughal aesthetics.
 
• Unlike Kathakali, Kathak does not typically involve elaborate makeup or costumes.
 
• It has a **strong emphasis on rhythm** and is performed both as a solo and in group settings.
 
 
 
• **Bharatanatyam:**
 
 
• Bharatanatyam is **one of the oldest classical dance forms from Tamil Nadu**, focusing on intricate footwork, hand gestures, and facial expressions.
 
• It often narrates religious and spiritual themes, primarily through the** depiction of Hindu deities.**
 
• The dance is performed by women and is known for its grace, fluid movements, and storytelling.
 
• Unlike Kathakali, it has less emphasis on vibrant makeup and elaborate costumes.
 
 
 
• **Manipuri:**
 
 
• Manipuri is a classical dance form originating from the** northeastern state of Manipur,** known for its graceful and flowing movements.
 
• It often depicts themes related to love and devotion,** particularly the Raas Leela (the divine dance of Lord Krishna).**
 
• The costumes are elegant but less elaborate compared to Kathakali, focusing more on fluidity and grace.
 
• Manipuri dance does not typically involve the dramatic makeup styles seen in Kathakali performances.

questions.question: _________ refers to buying and selling of bonds issued by the Government.
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Open Market Operations (OMO)** are the actions taken by a central bank to buy or sell government bonds in the open market.
 
• This process is used **to regulate the money supply** and influence interest rates in the economy.
 
• When the central bank buys bonds, it increases the money supply, making it easier for banks to lend money and potentially lowering interest rates.
 
• Conversely, **when it sells bonds, it decreases the money supply**, which can lead to higher interest rates.
 
• OMOs are a primary tool for monetary policy and are critical in managing economic stability.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Marginal Requirement:**

 
 
• Marginal requirement refers to the **minimum percentage of deposits** that banks are required to keep as reserves.
 
• It is not directly related to the buying or selling of government bonds.
 
• This requirement is set by the central bank and is** aimed at ensuring that banks maintain liquidity**.
 
• Changes in marginal requirements can affect the money supply and lending capacity of banks.
 
 
 
• **Closed Market Operations:**
 
 
• Closed Market Operations are not a standard term in monetary policy and typically** refer to scenarios where a central bank does not engage **in buying or selling government securities.
 
• It can** also imply a market **where there are **restrictions on the buying and selling **of government bonds.
 
• This term is less commonly used compared to open market operations.
 
 
 
• **Moral Suasion:**
 
 
• Moral suasion is a** non-coercive method used by central banks** to persuade banks and financial institutions to adhere to certain policies.
 
• It involves **communication and appeals** rather than direct action, such as buying or selling bonds.
 
• While it can influence monetary policy, it does not involve the actual trading of government bonds in the market.
 
• This approach** relies on the credibility of the central bank **to guide the financial behavior of institutions.

questions.question:
In Charles Law:

A) Pressure is kept constant

B) Number of moles of gas is constant

C) Volume is directly proportional to temperature

options.text: Both A and B is true
Both A and C is true
Only B and C is true

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**A, B, C are true**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **1787**, Jacques Charles formulated Charles' Law or the **Law of Volume**.
 
• According to this law,** at constant pressure, the volume of a given mass of gas is directly proportional to its temperature**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c0dadeb1c8ec4654752b6aff1fffaebede4ce14eabb92c1487e17ea58bf3032e.png] ​

**Explanation:**

 
• **Charle's law** is valid only when the pressure of the system is kept constant.
 
• Provided the pressure is kept constant, the gases when heated will achieve higher** kinetic energy**.
 
• The molecules' high kinetic energy will help them overcome their intermolecular forces and undergo expansion.
 
• Thus,** increasing the temperature**, the gases will undergo expansion, provided the pressure is kept constant.
 
• Decreasing the temperature, gases will undergo compression, and P kept constant.
 
• Hence, the **volume becomes directly proportional to temperature.**
 
• As volume depends on the pressure, altering it will thus cause a change in volume and the** effect of temperature** could not be understood.

Hence, Charles's law of observed at constant pressure.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Boyle's Law** states that for a fixed mass of gas at a constant temperature, the volume is inversely proportional to the pressure.
 
• **PV = constant**.
 
• Increasing or decreasing the pressure will thus cause a change in volume and the effect of temperature could not be understood.
 
• Gases that obey the gas laws (**Charles law, Boyles law, and Universal Gas Law**) are called **ideal gases**.
 
• **Gay-Lussac's law** states that at constant volume, **the pressure of a fixed amount of a gas varies directly with temperature.**

questions.question: The Indian political system is often described as a federal system with a strong unitary bias. Which feature gives it this unitary bias?

The correct answer is **__Single Citizenship.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Single Citizenship is defined as every citizen of India holds only one citizenship i.e. is of India rather than that of any state.
 
• This implies that all citizens share the same legal rights, obligations, and protections, promoting a unified national identity.
 
• Part II of Constitution incudes articles related to citizenship. These are: 
 
 
• **Article 5**: Provides for citizenship for individuals who were born in India or have Indian parents, and outlines the conditions for citizenship at the time of the Constitution's adoption in 1950.
 
• **Article 6**: Addresses the citizenship of people who migrated from Pakistan to India during the partition.
 
• **Article 7**: Covers those who migrated from India to Pakistan and later returned.
 
• **Article 8**: Provides for citizenship for individuals of Indian origin residing outside India.
 
• **Article 9**: States that anyone who voluntarily acquires citizenship of another country will lose Indian citizenship.
 
• **Articles 10 and 11**: Discuss the rights of citizenship and empower Parliament to make provisions for citizenship.
 
 
 
• Single citizenship fosters a sense of national identity and unity among the diverse population of India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Concurrent List** is enumerated in the **Seventh Schedule of the Indian Constitution**. 
 
• **Article ****246(2): **provides that both **Parliament and State Legislatures** can make laws relating to any of the matters enumerated in the Concurrent List.
 
• The Concurrent List originally had 47 items, but now it has 52 subjects ranging from** criminal law and procedure to marriage and divorce, bankruptcy and insolvency, trusts and trustees, and education**.
 
• The **State Lis**t is mentioned in the **Seventh Schedule** of the Indian Constitution.
 
• The State List contains** 66 subjects**.
 
• **Article 246(3)** provides that the legislature of any state has exclusive power to make laws with respect to any of the matters enumerated in the State List.
 
• **Dual citizenship** (or dual nationality) refers to the status of an individual who is a citizen of two different countries at the same time.
 
• **The Citizenship Act, 1955,** provides for the acquisition of Indian citizenship** by birth, descent, registration, naturalization, and incorporation of territory,** also **for renouncing or terminating Indian citizenship.**
 
• India does not permit dual citizenship.

**∴ The rate of interest per annum is 10%.**
